correctness.rationale: Deleting the hub gives the direct sum of grounded arms with the original degrees retained. In the lower Krylov columns the leading terms, in order, are u,Bu,…,B^(N−1)u; hub feedback only adds earlier columns with integer coefficients. For each arm the distance support of e₁,−D e₁,… gives a unit triangular basis. In those bases the block matrix is simultaneous remainder by the monic arm characteristic polynomials, with the argument sign changed for −D. To verify the pairwise product determinant, split off a monic factor P by writing f=r+Pq: the coordinate change is unit triangular up to ordering, the P-remainder is r, and the other remainders in q are multiplied by P. Each multiplication has determinant equal to the corresponding resultant, including zero when a factor is shared. The arm recurrence gives eigenangles (2j−1)π/(2ℓ+1). A common gcd g>1 gives the common angle π/g; if the odd labels are coprime, multiplication by the other odd label permutes the odd residues up to sign modulo 2(2ℓ+1), fixing the excluded odd residue 2ℓ+1. Thus the absolute numerator and denominator cosine products agree, giving resultant modulus one. This yields the integer index classification, not just an eigenvector test. The binomial translation to I−L is integral and unit triangular; column reversal is the n-step input map, and Cayley–Hamilton precludes recovery at a longer horizon if rank fails. In the full-rank case the symmetric spectrum is simple and the modal Vandermonde gives the stated finite-horizon determinant; its time kernel is positive definite by independence of distinct exponentials. Independent edge-by-edge Krylov recurrence and elimination modulo 1009 gave residues (1,0,0,1,1) for arms (1,2,3,5,6,8), (1,2,3,5,6,7), (2,7,9), (3,5,7,11), (4,5,6,8,9), unchanged by the shift. These residues are corroboration only; the packaged exact checker was inspected, not run.

value.rationale: A natural infinite family with genuine branching admits a complete exact gcd test for whether unbounded integer controls realize every integer state in n steps. A rank test cannot decide that lattice question, and the nonspider index-two example confirms that unimodularity is not automatic for unit trees. The output is useful without any claims about optimal placement, small input size or numerical conditioning.
